$comment: Test fixture exercising all fields of the africa-customary extension

customaryRules.daughterInheritanceRight: Equal share with sons per Reform Act 11 of 2009
Inherits through maternal line per Akan customary law

familyCouncilDecisions.decidedBy: Senior male elders of the Ndlovu family
familyCouncilDecisions.outcome: Eldest son appointed as customary heir with obligation to maintain the homestead

familyCouncilDecisions.decisionType: Distribution of livestock and household effects
familyCouncilDecisions.decidedBy: Extended family council including maternal uncle
familyCouncilDecisions.outcome: Livestock divided equally among sons; household effects allocated to surviving widow

communalPropertyDetails.notes: Land allocated by the traditional authority; no individual title deed exists. Permission to occupy (PTO) held by the deceased.

communalPropertyDetails.tenureType: Permission to occupy under KwaZulu-Natal traditional authority
communalPropertyDetails.notes: Grazing land allocated for communal use; not individually heritable under customary law

widowRights.customaryRight: Right to remain in the homestead and use household property
widowRights.statutoryRight: Full intestate inheritance right per Reform Act 11 of 2009
widowRights.ritesDescription: Traditional mourning period of one year observed, including wearing of mourning attire (inzilo) and cleansing ceremony (ukugeza)
widowRights.notes: Surviving first wife; customary and statutory rights both apply. Constitutional Court has upheld statutory protection.

widowRights.customaryRight: Usufructuary right over household allocated to her by the family council
widowRights.statutoryRight: Intestate share as surviving spouse under Intestate Succession Act
widowRights.ritesDescription: Traditional mourning rites pending; family council to confirm date
widowRights.notes: Surviving second wife in a customary marriage registered under the Recognition of Customary Marriages Act 120 of 1998

lobolaDetails.livestockDetails: 10 head of cattle delivered to the bride's family at Nongoma kraal; 4 cattle still outstanding
lobolaDetails.notes: Lobola negotiations concluded in 2010. Outstanding balance of R40,000 and 4 cattle to be settled from the estate before distribution.

landTenureDetails.tenureType: Communal tenure under Ingonyama Trust Board
landTenureDetails.communityAuthority: Inkosi Mthembu, Traditional Authority of KwaNongoma
landTenureDetails.notes: Homestead site allocated by the traditional council in 1995; no formal title deed
Former communal land converted to individual freehold under the Upgrading of Land Tenure Rights Act 112 of 1991

constitutionalChallenges.description: Challenge to the principle of male primogeniture in customary succession as violating the right to equality under section 9 of the Constitution
constitutionalChallenges.notes: Constitutional Court declared the rule of male primogeniture in customary law of succession unconstitutional

constitutionalChallenges.description: Challenge to exclusion of extra-marital children from customary inheritance
constitutionalChallenges.notes: Appeal pending before the Supreme Court of Appeal; interim order grants maintenance from the estate

notes: Estate of a Zulu man domiciled in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Two customary marriages registered under the Recognition of Customary Marriages Act. The Reform of Customary Law of Succession Act 11 of 2009 applies, overriding male primogeniture. Communal land held under the Ingonyama Trust.

x-inherit-traditional-authority.value: KwaNongoma Traditional Council, under Inkosi Mthembu
